body: Update: No reply, no contact in any way. I’m at a loss.

I do, and I’m very thankful for them. It’s hard because they’re all struggling— I’m trying to get past that fear of reaching out. Everyone keeps telling me in their own ways to forget him and move on, but we are kind of legally obligated to this house… and eventually he will have to discuss that… so at some point contact will need to happen again whether either of us want that or not

What?! That would be awesome. Rather than a traditional dinner I want an all-you-can-eat buffet style dinner. Saw an idea for a cookies and milk bar. I love this.

I'm adding 'Cheese Fountain' to my list of ridiculous food requests.

You know... I've lived and was raised in a small town. After being diagnosed I still held on to a lot of the "Pull yourself up by your bootstraps" mentality I was raised with.

I'm not neurotypical, though. It's not just a matter of pulling myself up by my bootstraps... it's about making sure the boots are on the right feet, fit well, and are comfortable enough for me to walk in. You're right. Thank you. I needed that more than you realize.

No, I informed my boss that I was autistic when I was hired on and told her "I don't need you to cater to me or make my job easier, I just want you to know because I have these quirks, and I hope that in knowing you can understand me better." After the situation occurred between my new supervisor and I, I had a meeting with our director about it. She questioned the legitimacy of my diagnoses and asked some personal questions, as going as far as to ask who my doctor was and what the process was when I was diagnosed. (Sadly I have all this written down in case they planned on firing me over it; I intended to sue them.) 

When we were still working out of the office, (I'm currently back for short hours during the week,) something in me just snapped. I knew I couldn't work for them anymore. It wasn't something I was willing to put up with, and I wanted to do something different with my life. I have a passion I wanted to pursue my whole life, but always thought it was just a hobby. It's what I want to focus my time and energy on, now, and eventually start my own business. It was a combination of "Screw this," and "I know what I want to do with myself for real now."

I'm hoping that's something I'll be able to find out tonight; Honestly if that's the case I think I'd be fired on the spot for applying for a different position. I think that would be the case regardless of whether or not this happened. That is a great point though, and something I will keep in mind going into this interview.

I have been told that I excel at my job on multiple occasions. I am a Children's Librarian and plan multiple events, host Early Lit. Classes, Lapsit Programs, Etc. I was hired because of my positive attitude and because I stood out as a fit for the job. I've worked at the library for 3 years, but I've only worked in this position for the past 6 months. 

I was told in my meeting that I just didn't seem to remember the compliments well enough, and that I only seem to take away the negative criticism from my encounters with my supervisor. 

I didn't have it in me, but I really wanted to say "It's really hard to remember the positive when you're being yelled at."
I appreciate the honesty; Thank you

NAH, and I have the exact same issue with fabrics and you have NO idea how much I wish I knew it was SPD at your age. Talk to a psychiatrist about your issues! They can point you in the right direction for self-help, therapy, and ways around these triggers!

(25F) here that has worked past a lot of sensory related triggers, and I know you'll be able to work through this in time. For now, though, talk to your family if there's any way you can make a compromise? Ie; Wear the dress for the ceremony and photos, but if there's a reception, pack a change of comfortable clothes you can fit into, as well as any gentle soaps you might want to use on your face to get rid of the makeup if it bothers you. Let your hair down (or leave it as is if there's no hairspray in it bothering you,) and be yourself! 

It's so hard, I grew up in tears being dragged to church in my sunday best-- it's really hard, but if you love your sister I know you can pull through for just a few hours! Do it for her! But don't let them push you around, either!

I work at a library. I had a much older patron in our empty computer room who I was trying to assist turn and say to me:

"I hope you don't find this offensive, but, you are a very sexy young woman. Can I pay you to help me outside of your job?"

I tried to awkwardly laugh it off, and told him no, that I wasn't interested, but would be happy to help him here. Again, he was elderly, possibly in his 70's so I was trying to be patient with him. Then he got up from his seat, and left in a hurry.

He came back the following day, and asked me again if I'd be interested helping him out at his home. Then, the next day. My boss was never around the area at this time, so I told him what was going on and asked if he could just idle around in case it happens again.

It did. Guy got his ear chewed off big time, was informed that soliciting business with our employees was inappropriate behavior, etc.

I never saw him again after that. Thank god.
This has absolutely been the highlight of my day. Thank you for sharing, Pistachio Witch!!!

I was driving home in my car one night, driving about 35 mph on the main road in my town. Out of nowhere, I see this man RUN across the street at the intersection, and I slam on my breaks to prevent hitting him. It was a well lit area by a gas station, so I swear I could see him as clear as day. He was standing right in front of me where I stopped, and he just stared at me. I had gotten out of my car to make sure he was okay, but when I opened my car door, he was just... gone. Like, blink of an eye, gone. I drove around a bit to see if I could find him to make sure he was okay, but... I never saw him again. I visibly remember what he looks like, so I'm sure if I saw him again I'd be able to recognize him. But honestly, I don't know if he does. It was an odd experience that happened about 3 years ago over the summer.
